title: The delist-aware restock surface: the opt-in miss, the suppression, and the relist release
note: Authored from the committed blob at the fix commit, before any replay ran, with claimed_count deliberately absent: this is the FIRST recording, so the replay that follows is the figures' origin, not a re-check. The fix has three load-bearing halves and each is broken here the way a regression would actually break it: M1 removes the opt-in gate so a delisted slug answers the same 201 an active one does - the existence leak the 404-on-detail behaviour one endpoint over exists to refuse; M2 removes the fan-out's is_active re-check so a restock that lands while the product is off sale mails 'Back in stock' with a link to a 404 detail page; M3 drops the relist registration so the deferral decision (suppress while inactive, release on relist) loses its symmetric half and a customer who opted in before a delist is silenced for good.

mutations.description: the opt-in surface stops refusing delisted products: the is_active gate is dead, so a delisted slug answers the same 201 an active one does, leaking that the product exists (and its product_id) against a 404 for an unknown slug

the fan-out loses its is_active re-check, so a restock that lands while the product is delisted mails 'Back in stock' linking a detail page that 404s - the exact customer-facing defect the fix exists to close

the relist action stops registering the release, so the suppression's symmetric half is gone: waiting opt-ins from before a delist are never told the product came back, which is deliberate silence rather than deferral
